steps.message: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Ruby on Rails application. Start in the `/app` Git repository. It has no app yet. Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Time for the main feature: the live game.

A quiz can be played many times (for example, a rehearsal and the real talk). Each time is a new game with its own players and answers. Games skip inactive questions.

The moderator's side:

- The quiz page gets the "Start a game" button. It creates a new game and opens its big-screen page for the moderator (it stays in the moderator area).
- Before the start, the big screen shows the quiz title, the join link as plain text, a QR code with the same link, and the number of players currently waiting for the quiz to start as "Players: 2". The join link is a full URL; the scheme can be left out (for example, `localhost:3000/play/K7RZX`).
- The "Start" button shows the first active question: the progress ("Question 1 of 3"), the question text, and the options. While the question is open, the big screen counts the players who answered as "Answers: 1 / 2" (players who answered / players currently in the game). The second counter is important for moderators 'cause it shows if they need to wait for more answers or not, are there any active players in the game.
- The "Finish" button closes the question. The big screen then shows the number of answers for each option and marks the correct options with "Correct".
- The "Next" button shows the next active question. On the last question, the button is "End quiz" instead, and it ends the game.
- After the end, the big screen shows "The quiz is over".

The player's side:

- A player opens the join link on a phone. No account is needed: the page asks for "Your name" and has the "Join" button. After joining, the player sees "Hi, <name>!" (for example, "Hi, Alice!") and waits for the start.
- The browser remembers the player: opening the join link again in the same browser continues the game as the same player.
- Players can join at any time before the end. After the end, the join link shows "The quiz is over" and does not let anyone join.
- During a question, the player sees the question text and its options as buttons. Tapping an option submits it at once, and the option is marked "Your answer". The player can change the answer until the question is closed; the last pick counts. Players must not be able to find out the correct answer, not even in the page source, before the question is closed.
- After "Finish", the player sees "Correct!", "Wrong!", or "No answer".
- After the end, the player sees "The quiz is over".

Everything is live: the big screen, the counters, and the phones follow the game without page reloads. Participants typically use crowded conference Wi-Fi.

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# Quizzy Architecture & Design Notes

## Runtime & Deployment

- **Entrypoint**: `bin/serve` prepares SQLite (`bin/rails db:prepare`), compiles Propshaft assets (`bin/rails assets:clobber assets:precompile`), and runs Puma in the foreground listening on `0.0.0.0:${PORT}`.
- **Plain HTTP & Host Independence**: `config.assume_ssl = false`, `config.force_ssl = false`, `config.hosts.clear`, and `config.public_file_server.enabled = true` ensure the app works over plain HTTP on any conference network hostname without external dependencies.
- **Storage**: All persistent state lives under `storage/` (`storage/production.sqlite3`).
- **Health Check**: `GET /up` returns `200` without authentication.

## Authentication

- All moderator routes live under `/moderate` and inherit from `Moderate::BaseController`.
- `Moderate::BaseController` enforces HTTP Basic Authentication comparing against `ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME"]` and `ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD"]` using SHA-256 digests with `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`. Empty credentials are always rejected (`401`).

## Data Model (Release 1)

- `Quiz` (`quizzes`): `title` (required, whitespace-normalized). `has_many :questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy`.
- `Question` (`questions`): `quiz_id`, `body` (required, whitespace-normalized), `position` (integer ordering), `active` (boolean, default `true`). `has_many :options, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy`.
- `Option` (`options`): `question_id`, `title` (required, whitespace-normalized), `correct` (boolean, default `false`), `position` (integer ordering).
- `Question#save_with_options` validates `body` and the filtered non-empty option rows (at least 2 options, at least 1 marked correct) before touching the database, preserving all submitted rows (including blanks) in memory if validation fails.
- `Question#move!(direction)` atomically swaps adjacent positions and normalizes `position` to `1..N` inside a transaction.

## Quiz Export & Import

- **Export**: `GET /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/export` (`Moderate::ExportsController#show`) renders `Quiz#to_export_json` inside a single `<pre class="code-block">` element.
  - `Quiz#export_data` writes strictly `title`, `questions` (`text`, `active`, `options`), and each option (`text`, `correct`) in position order, with no IDs, timestamps, or runtime data. Both `active` and `correct` are always emitted as explicit booleans.
- **Import**: `GET /moderate/import` and `POST /moderate/import` (`Moderate::QuizImportsController`) use the `QuizImport` `ActiveModel::Model` form object (`app/models/quiz_import.rb`).
  - Validates the full JSON structure and all question rules (non-blank title/texts, strict booleans when `active`/`correct` are present, defaults `active: true` and `correct: false` when omitted, >= 2 options per question, >= 1 correct option per question) before writing inside a single `Quiz.transaction`, guaranteeing all-or-nothing atomicity.
  - Always creates a new `Quiz` record (even if another quiz shares the title) and redirects to the new quiz page.

## Frontend & Design System

- **Assets**: `app/assets/stylesheets/quizzy.css` and `app/assets/fonts/Inter-latin.woff2` are sourced directly from `docs/mockups/`, compiled locally via Propshaft with zero external network calls.
- **Stimulus Controllers** (via Importmap, local vendored gems):
  - `option_rows_controller.js`: Dynamically adds/removes option rows and maintains contiguous numbering (`Option 1`, `Option 1 is correct`, etc.).
  - `question_active_controller.js`: Saves the `"Active"` checkbox immediately via `PATCH .../active` (`fetch` with `keepalive: true`), updating question numbering and active counts in place.
  - `preview_controller.js`: Runs the interactive quiz preview purely client-side over the quiz's active questions in order; preview answers are never persisted.
- **Accessibility & QA Compatibility**:
  - Lists use semantic `<ul>`/`<ol>` with each quiz/question in its own `<li>` containing its actions.
  - Icon-only buttons (`Move up`, `Move down`) use `aria-label` and `title` with `aria-hidden="true"` on glyphs.
  - Decorative CSS pseudo-elements (`+ ` on `Add option`, `Correct` on option checkboxes) use CSS Content Level 3 empty alt text (`content: "..." / ""`) so exact accessible names remain clean.
  - Destructive confirmations use native browser `confirm()` via Turbo (`data-turbo-confirm`).

## Notes for Future Releases (Live Runs, Big Screen, Phones)

- **Live Runs & Snapshots**: Currently `Question#save_with_options` replaces `options` via `delete_all` + `create!`. When live runs and participant answers are added, either snapshot questions/options per run or upsert options by `id` (and avoid deleting referenced options) so historical answers stay intact. Keep `Quiz#export_data` strictly scoped to quiz contents (`title`, `questions`, `options`) so live run/game data is never exported.
- **Real-time Updates**: ActionCable is enabled with the `async` adapter in single-process Puma (`config/cable.yml`), ready for broadcasting stage/question/reveal state to big screens and player phones without Redis.
- **Shared Styles**: `quizzy.css` already includes the `.screen`, `.cover`, `.lobby`, `.stage-option`, `.leaderboard`, `.play`, and `.response-*` classes for big-screen presentation, phone play, and moderator response summaries.

class Question < ApplicationRecord
  DEFAULT_OPTION_ROWS = 4

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :options, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy

  scope :ordered, -> { order(:position, :id) }
  scope :active, -> { where(active: true) }

  normalizes :body, with: ->(text) { text.strip }

  validates :body, presence: true
  validates :position, presence: true, numericality: { only_integer: true }

  def form_option_rows
    if defined?(@submitted_option_rows) && @submitted_option_rows.present?
      return @submitted_option_rows
    end

    if persisted?
      options.map { |opt| { title: opt.title, correct: opt.correct } }
    else
      Array.new(DEFAULT_OPTION_ROWS) { { title: "", correct: false } }
    end
  end

  def save_with_options(raw_rows)
    @submitted_option_rows = normalize_submitted_rows(raw_rows)
    non_empty_rows = @submitted_option_rows.reject { |row| row[:title].strip.empty? }

    assign_next_position if position.nil?

    valid?

    errors.add(:base, "Add at least two options") if non_empty_rows.size < 2
    errors.add(:base, "Mark at least one option as correct") if non_empty_rows.none? { |row| row[:correct] }

    return false if errors.any?

    transaction do
      assign_next_position if new_record?
      save!
      options.delete_all
      non_empty_rows.each_with_index do |row, index|
        options.create!(
          title: row[:title].strip,
          correct: row[:correct],
          position: index + 1
        )
      end
    end

    true
  end

  def move!(direction)
    return false unless persisted?

    transaction do
      ordered_questions = quiz.questions.ordered.to_a
      idx = ordered_questions.index(self)
      return false unless idx

      target_idx =
        case direction.to_s
        when "up" then idx - 1
        when "down" then idx + 1
        else return false
        end

      return false if target_idx.negative? || target_idx >= ordered_questions.length

      ordered_questions[idx], ordered_questions[target_idx] =
        ordered_questions[target_idx], ordered_questions[idx]

      ordered_questions.each_with_index do |question, index|
        new_pos = index + 1
        question.update_column(:position, new_pos) if question.position != new_pos
      end
    end

    true
  end

  private

  def assign_next_position
    self.position = (quiz.questions.maximum(:position) || 0) + 1
  end

  def normalize_submitted_rows(raw_rows)
    entries =
      case raw_rows
      when ActionController::Parameters
        raw_rows.to_h.sort_by { |k, _| k.to_i }.map(&:last)
      when Hash
        raw_rows.sort_by { |k, _| k.to_i }.map(&:last)
      when Array
        raw_rows
      else
        []
      end

    boolean_type = ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new

    entries.map do |entry|
      hash = entry.respond_to?(:to_h) ? entry.to_h.with_indifferent_access : {}
      {
        title: hash[:title].to_s,
        correct: boolean_type.cast(hash[:correct]) == true
      }
    end
  end
end

export default class extends Controller {

    if (this.answered) return

    const button = event.currentTarget
    const optionIndex = Number(button.dataset.optionIndex)
    const question = this.questionsValue[this.currentIndex]
    const picked = question?.options?.[optionIndex]
    if (!picked) return

    this.answered = true

    if (picked.correct) {
      this.score += 1
      this.statusTarget.textContent = "Correct!"
      this.statusTarget.className = "play-status play-status--right"
    } else {
      this.statusTarget.textContent = "Wrong!"
      this.statusTarget.className = "play-status play-status--wrong"
    }
    this.statusTarget.hidden = false

    this.optionsTarget.classList.add("is-locked", "is-revealed")

    const buttons = this.optionsTarget.querySelectorAll("button.play-option")
    buttons.forEach((btn, idx) => {
      const opt = question.options[idx]
      const mark = btn.querySelector(".play-option__mark")
      btn.disabled = true

      if (idx === optionIndex) {
        btn.classList.add("is-picked")
      }

      if (opt.correct) {
        btn.classList.add("is-correct")
        btn.dataset.correct = "true"
        if (mark) mark.textContent = "✓ Correct"
      } else if (idx === optionIndex) {
        if (mark) mark.textContent = "✕"
      }
    })

    const isLast = this.currentIndex >= this.questionsValue.length - 1
    this.nextButtonTarget.hidden = isLast
    this.scoreButtonTarget.hidden = !isLast
    this.actionsTarget.hidden = false
  }

  next() {
    if (!this.answered) return
    if (this.currentIndex >= this.questionsValue.length - 1) return

    this.currentIndex += 1
    this.answered = false
    this.renderQuestion()
  }

  showScore() {
    if (!this.answered) return

    const total = this.questionsValue.length
    this.scoreBigTarget.textContent = `${this.score}/${total}`
    this.scoreTextTarget.textContent = `Score: ${this.score}/${total}`

    this.questionViewTarget.hidden = true
    this.scoreViewTarget.hidden = false
    if (this.hasBannerRestartTarget) {
      this.bannerRestartTarget.hidden = true
    }
  }

  restart() {
    this.currentIndex = 0
    this.score = 0
    this.answered = false

    this.scoreViewTarget.hidden = true
    this.questionViewTarget.hidden = false
    if (this.hasBannerRestartTarget) {
      this.bannerRestartTarget.hidden = false
    }

    this.renderQuestion()
  }

  renderQuestion() {
    const total = this.questionsValue.length
    const question = this.questionsValue[this.currentIndex]
    if (!question) return

    this.progressTarget.textContent = `Question ${this.currentIndex + 1} of ${total}`
    this.questionBodyTarget.textContent = question.body

    this.optionsTarget.className = "play-options"
    this.optionsTarget.replaceChildren()

    question.options.forEach((option, index) => {
      const btn = document.createElement("button")
      btn.type = "button"
      btn.className = "play-option"
      btn.dataset.action = "preview#pick"
      btn.dataset.optionIndex = String(index)

      const letter = document.createElement("span")
      letter.className = "play-option__letter"
      letter.setAttribute("aria-hidden", "true")
      letter.textContent = this.optionLetter(index)

      const title = document.createElement("span")
      title.className = "play-option__title"
      title.textContent = option.title

      const mark = document.createElement("span")
      mark.className = "play-option__mark"

      btn.append(letter, title, mark)
      this.optionsTarget.appendChild(btn)
    })

    this.statusTarget.hidden = true
    this.statusTarget.textContent = ""
    this.actionsTarget.hidden = true
    this.nextButtonTarget.hidden = true
    this.scoreButtonTarget.hidden = true
  }

  optionLetter(index) {
    let n = index + 1
    let result = ""
    while (n > 0) {

      result = String.fromCharCode(65 + (n % 26)) + result
      n = Math.floor(n / 26)

import { Controller } from "@hotwired/stimulus"

export default class extends Controller {
  static targets = ["summary", "item"]

  async toggle(event) {
    const checkbox = event.currentTarget
    const form = checkbox.closest("form")
    const item = checkbox.closest("[data-question-active-target='item']")
    const active = checkbox.checked

    checkbox.defaultChecked = active
    if (item) {
      item.classList.toggle("question-item--inactive", !active)
    }

    const csrfToken = document.querySelector("meta[name='csrf-token']")?.content

    try {
      const response = await fetch(form.action, {
        method: "PATCH",
        credentials: "same-origin",
        headers: {
          "Content-Type": "application/json",
          "Accept": "application/json",
          ...(csrfToken ? { "X-CSRF-Token": csrfToken } : {})
        },
        body: JSON.stringify({ question: { active } }),
        keepalive: true
      })

      if (!response.ok) {
        throw new Error(`HTTP ${response.status}`)
      }

      const data = await response.json()
      this.applyServerState(data)
    } catch (_error) {
      checkbox.checked = !active
      checkbox.defaultChecked = !active
      if (item) {
        item.classList.toggle("question-item--inactive", active)
      }
    }
  }

  applyServerState(data) {
    if (this.hasSummaryTarget) {
      const word = data.total_count === 1 ? "question" : "questions"
      this.summaryTarget.textContent = `${data.active_count} of ${data.total_count} ${word} active`
    }

      const number = data.numbers?.[id]
      const numEl = item.querySelector("[data-role='num']")
      if (numEl) {

Let's start with `GamePresence` – need to drill down into the interaction of `register` and `unregister` with `PlayerGameChannel`. If `register` is called in `subscribed` and `unregister` in `unsubscribed`, what's the behavior? Thinking this through… When `register` runs it returns the new count of players and whether anything changed. And when the background reaper thread runs, finding expired `conn_id`s across all games, deleting them, collecting the counts and broadcasting the updates outside the mutex is what we want.

I need to also consider HTTP fallback polling. The `PlayController#state` receives a specific header when the WebSocket disconnects. It calls `GamePresence.heartbeat` and if it changed, broadcasts. The cool part is when the WebSocket connects again, `PlayerGameChannel#subscribed` can pass the `fallback_client_id` and unregister it while registering the WebSocket connection immediately, avoiding overlap and stale HTTP entries.

Wow! Using a per-tab ID (like a UUID or random string) for WebSocket connections as the `conn_id`, and the SAME ID for HTTP fallback means a clean transition. When the WebSocket connects, the `tabId` entry overwrites it with `STALE_AFTER`. And, when the WebSocket cleanly closes, `unregister` removes it immediately. Zero duplicate entries, and a smooth transition even with temporary HTTP fallback.

Next, I'll need to look at broadcasting. In `Game#broadcast_state!`, it's three streams: moderator, players, and, if the game's ended, a specific stream to communicate the "ended" status on the join page. Don't forget that after broadcasting the "ended" status, `GamePresence.clear_game!` can run to free memory cleanly.

Then, there's `Game#record_answer!`. I need to verify how `Answer.upsert` with `unique_by:` and `update_only:` works in Rails 8.1 with SQLite. I need to test that behavior.

I will also review how atomic updates are handled in `Game#start!`, `Game#finish_question!`, `Game#next_question!`, and `Game#end_game!`. I need to ensure SQLite transactions use `transaction` for locking, to avoid any race conditions. These atomic conditional updates are neat! Even with simultaneous HTTP requests hitting a "next" endpoint, only one will succeed and the others will correctly return the current state, preventing double advancements.

cat <<'EOF' > app/models/game_presence.rb
class GamePresence
  STALE_AFTER = 15.0
  HTTP_FALLBACK_TTL = 6.0
  REAP_INTERVAL = 5.0

  @mutex = Mutex.new
  @games = {}
  @reaper_thread = nil

  class << self
    def register(game_id, player_id, connection_id, ttl: STALE_AFTER)
      update_entry(game_id.to_i, player_id.to_i, connection_id.to_s, ttl: ttl)
    end

    def heartbeat(game_id, player_id, connection_id, ttl: STALE_AFTER)
      update_entry(game_id.to_i, player_id.to_i, connection_id.to_s, ttl: ttl)
    end

    def unregister(game_id, player_id, connection_id)
      gid = game_id.to_i
      pid = player_id.to_i
      cid = connection_id.to_s

      @mutex.synchronize do
        now = monotonic_now
        prune_game_locked(gid, now)

        game_map = @games[gid]
        return [ 0, false ] unless game_map

        before_count = game_map.size
        player_conns = game_map[pid]
        if player_conns
          player_conns.delete(cid)
          game_map.delete(pid) if player_conns.empty?
        end
        @games.delete(gid) if game_map.empty?

        after_count = @games[gid]&.size || 0
        [ after_count, after_count != before_count ]
      end
    end

    def player_count(game_id)
      gid = game_id.to_i
      @mutex.synchronize do
        prune_game_locked(gid, monotonic_now)
        @games[gid]&.size || 0
      end
    end

    def clear_game!(game_id)
      gid = game_id.to_i
      @mutex.synchronize do
        @games.delete(gid)
      end
    end

    def reap_expired!
      changes = []
      @mutex.synchronize do
        now = monotonic_now
        @games.keys.each do |gid|
          before_count = @games[gid].size
          prune_game_locked(gid, now)
          after_count = @games[gid]&.size || 0
          changes << [ gid, after_count ] if after_count != before_count
        end
      end

      changes.each do |gid, count|
        ActionCable.server.broadcast(
          Game.moderator_stream_name(gid),
          { type: "presence", players_count: count }
        )
      end

      changes
    end

    def reset!
      @mutex.synchronize do
        @games.clear
      end
    end

    private

    def update_entry(gid, pid, cid, ttl:)
      @mutex.synchronize do
        now = monotonic_now
        prune_game_locked(gid, now)

        game_map = (@games[gid] ||= {})
        before_count = game_map.size

        player_conns = (game_map[pid] ||= {})
        player_conns[cid] = now + ttl.to_f

        after_count = game_map.size
        ensure_reaper_running_locked
        [ after_count, after_count != before_count ]
      end
    end

    def prune_game_locked(gid, now)
      game_map = @games[gid]
      return unless game_map

      game_map.each do |pid, conns|
        conns.delete_if { |_cid, expires_at| expires_at <= now }
      end
      game_map.delete_if { |_pid, conns| conns.empty? }
      @games.delete(gid) if game_map.empty?
    end

    def ensure_reaper_running_locked
      return if @reaper_thread&.alive?

      @reaper_thread = Thread.new do
        loop do
          sleep REAP_INTERVAL
          reap_expired!
        rescue StandardError => e
          Rails.logger.error("[GamePresence] reaper error: #{e.class}: #{e.message}")
        end
      end
    end

    def monotonic_now
      Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
    end
  end
end
EOF

cat <<'EOF' > app/models/game.rb
class Game < ApplicationRecord
  STATUSES = %w[lobby question reveal ended].freeze
  CODE_ALPHABET = %w[A B C D E F G H J K M N P Q R S T U V W X Y Z 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9].freeze
  CODE_LENGTH = 5

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :answers, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :players, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :game_questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy

  validates :code, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validates :status, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }

  class << self
    def find_by_code(raw_code)
      normalized = raw_code.to_s.strip.upcase
      return nil if normalized.empty?

      find_by(code: normalized)
    end

    def create_for_quiz!(quiz)
      active_questions = quiz.active_questions.to_a
      return nil if active_questions.empty?

      transaction do
        game = quiz.games.create!(code: generate_unique_code, status: "lobby")
        active_questions.each_with_index do |question, q_index|
          gq = game.game_questions.create!(
            question_id: question.id,
            body: question.body,
            position: q_index + 1
          )
          question.options.each_with_index do |option, o_index|
            gq.game_options.create!(
              title: option.title,
              correct: option.correct?,
              position: o_index + 1
            )
          end
        end
        game
      end
    end

    def moderator_stream_name(game_id)
      "game:#{game_id}:moderator"
    end

    def players_stream_name(game_id)
      "game:#{game_id}:players"
    end

    def player_stream_name(game_id, player_id)
      "game:#{game_id}:player:#{player_id}"
    end

    def join_status_stream_name(game_id)
      "game:#{game_id}:join_status"
    end

    private

    def generate_unique_code
      loop do
        candidate = Array.new(CODE_LENGTH) { CODE_ALPHABET[SecureRandom.random_number(CODE_ALPHABET.length)] }.join
        return candidate unless exists?(code: candidate)
      end
    end
  end

  def lobby?
    status == "lobby"
  end

  def question?
    status == "question"
  end

  def reveal?
    status == "reveal"
  end

  def ended?
    status == "ended"
  end

  def total_questions
    @total_questions ||= game_questions.count
  end

  def current_question
    return nil if current_question_position.nil?

    game_questions.includes(:game_options).find_by(position: current_question_position)
  end

  def last_question?
    current_question_position.present? && current_question_position >= total_questions
  end

  def moderator_stream_token
    signed_id(purpose: :moderator_channel, expires_in: 24.hours)
  end

  def start!
    changed = false
    transaction do
      return false unless game_questions.exists?

      updated = self.class.where(id: id, status: "lobby").update_all(
        status: "question",
        current_question_position: 1,
        started_at: Time.current,
        updated_at: Time.current
      )
      changed = updated == 1
    end

    reload
    @total_questions = nil
    broadcast_state! if changed
    changed
  end

  def finish_question!(expected_position: nil)
    changed = false
    transaction do
      reload
      return false unless question?
      return false if expected_position.present? && current_question_position != expected_position.to_i

      updated = self.class.where(
        id: id,
        status: "question",
        current_question_position: current_question_position
      ).update_all(
        status: "reveal",
        updated_at: Time.current
      )
      changed = updated == 1
    end

    reload
    broadcast_state! if changed
    changed
  end

  def next_question!(expected_position: nil)
    changed = false
    transaction do
      reload
      return false unless reveal? && !last_question?
      return false if expected_position.present? && current_question_position != expected_position.to_i

      from_pos = current_question_position
      updated = self.class.where(
        id: id,
        status: "reveal",
        current_question_position: from_pos
      ).update_all(
        status: "question",
        current_question_position: from_pos + 1,
        updated_at: Time.current
      )
      changed = updated == 1
    end

    reload
    broadcast_state! if changed
    changed
  end

  def end_game!
    changed = false
    transaction do
      updated = self.class.where(id: id).where.not(status: "ended").update_all(
        status: "ended",
        ended_at: Time.current,
        updated_at: Time.current
      )
      changed = updated == 1
    end

    reload
    if changed
      broadcast_state!
      GamePresence.clear_game!(id)
    end
    changed
  end

  def record_answer!(player:, game_question_id:, game_option_id:)
    saved = false
    selected_id = nil
    question_id = nil

    transaction do
      reload
      return { ok: false, state: player_state(player) } unless question?

      q = current_question
      return { ok: false, state: player_state(player) } unless q && q.id == game_question_id.to_i

      option = q.game_options.find_by(id: game_option_id)
      return { ok: false, state: player_state(player) } unless option

      now = Time.current
      Answer.upsert(
        {
          game_id: id,
          player_id: player.id,
          game_question_id: q.id,
          game_option_id: option.id,
          created_at: now,
          updated_at: now
        },
        unique_by: %i[ player_id game_question_id ],
        update_only: %i[ game_option_id updated_at ]
      )

      saved = true
      selected_id = option.id
      question_id = q.id
    end

    if saved
      broadcast_counts!
      broadcast_player_selection!(player.id, question_id, selected_id)
      { ok: true, game_question_id: question_id, selected_option_id: selected_id }
    else
      { ok: false, state: player_state(player) }
    end
  end

  def current_question_answers_count
    q = current_question
    return 0 unless q

    answers.where(game_question_id: q.id).count
  end

  def moderator_state
    q = current_question
    players_count = GamePresence.player_count(id)

    payload = {
      type: "state",
      game_id: id,
      code: code,
      quiz_title: quiz.title,
      status: status,
      total_questions: total_questions,
      current_question_position: current_question_position,
      is_last_question: last_question?,
      players_count: players_count,
      answers_count: q ? answers.where(game_question_id: q.id).count : 0,
      question: nil
    }

    if q && (question? || reveal?)
      if reveal?
        counts_by_option = answers.where(game_question_id: q.id).group(:game_option_id).count
        total_answers = counts_by_option.values.sum
        payload[:question] = {
          id: q.id,
          position: q.position,
          total: total_questions,
          body: q.body,
          total_answers: total_answers,
          options: q.game_options.map do |opt|
            count = counts_by_option.fetch(opt.id, 0)
            {
              id: opt.id,
              title: opt.title,
              position: opt.position,
              correct: opt.correct?,
              count: count,
              share: total_answers.positive? ? ((count * 100.0) / total_answers).round : 0
            }
          end
        }
      else
        payload[:question] = {
          id: q.id,
          position: q.position,
          total: total_questions,
          body: q.body,
          options: q.game_options.map do |opt|
            {
              id: opt.id,
              title: opt.title,
              position: opt.position
            }
          end
        }
      end
    end

    payload
  end

  # Public broadcast state sent to all connected players.
  # STRICT SECURITY INVARIANT: Never includes `correct` flags while status is "lobby" or "question"!
  def player_broadcast_state
    case status
    when "lobby"
      { type: "state", status: "lobby" }
    when "question"
      q = current_question
      {
        type: "state",
        status: "question",
        question: q ? {
          id: q.id,
          position: q.position,
          total: total_questions,
          body: q.body,
          options: q.game_options.map do |opt|
            {
              id: opt.id,
              title: opt.title,
              position: opt.position
            }
          end
        } : nil
      }
    when "reveal"
      q = current_question
      {
        type: "state",
        status: "reveal",
        question: q ? {
          id: q.id,
          position: q.position,
          total: total_questions,
          body: q.body,
          options: q.game_options.map do |opt|
            {
              id: opt.id,
              title: opt.title,
              position: opt.position,
              correct: opt.correct?
            }
          end
        } : nil
      }
    else
      { type: "state", status: "ended" }
    end
  end

  # Personalized state for a specific player (initial render, WS subscribe resync, HTTP state).
  # STRICT SECURITY INVARIANT: Never includes `correct` flags before status is "reveal"!
  def player_state(player)
    payload = player_broadcast_state.merge(player_name: player.name)

    if (question? || reveal?) && (q = current_question)
      answer = answers.includes(:game_option).find_by(player_id: player.id, game_question_id: q.id)
      payload[:selected_option_id] = answer&.game_option_id

      if reveal?
        payload[:result] =
          if answer.nil?
            "no_answer"
          elsif answer.game_option.correct?
            "correct"
          else
            "wrong"
          end
      end
    end

    payload
  end

  def broadcast_state!
    ActionCable.server.broadcast(self.class.moderator_stream_name(id), moderator_state)
    ActionCable.server.broadcast(self.class.players_stream_name(id), player_broadcast_state)
    if ended?
      ActionCable.server.broadcast(self.class.join_status_stream_name(id), { type: "state", status: "ended" })
    end
  end

  def broadcast_presence!(players_count = GamePresence.player_count(id))
    ActionCable.server.broadcast(
      self.class.moderator_stream_name(id),
      { type: "presence", players_count: players_count }
    )
  end

  def broadcast_counts!
    ActionCable.server.broadcast(
      self.class.moderator_stream_name(id),
      {
        type: "counts",
        answers_count: current_question_answers_count,
        players_count: GamePresence.player_count(id)
      }
    )
  end

  def broadcast_player_selection!(player_id, game_question_id, selected_option_id)
    ActionCable.server.broadcast(
      self.class.player_stream_name(id, player_id),
      {
        type: "selection",
        game_question_id: game_question_id,
        selected_option_id: selected_option_id
      }
    )
  end
end

**ActionCable Channels: Deep Dive and Edge Case Considerations**

Okay, this is fantastic! Everything, and I mean *everything*, from model operations like creating the game and updating answers, all the way to handling game destruction, worked flawlessly on the first try. That's a huge win!

Now, it's time to build out ActionCable Channels for this thing. I'm going to meticulously check every detail of each of these five files: `application_cable/connection.rb`, `application_cable/channel.rb`, `moderator_game_channel.rb`, `player_game_channel.rb`, and `join_status_channel.rb`.

Wait a minute, let's zoom in on `PlayerGameChannel`. There are some subtle, but critical, edge cases I need to address. First: What if a player tries to connect to the channel *after* the game has ended? I need to make sure I don't reject them, but instead immediately transmit the game state indicating the game is over and their player name, and, very important, don't register them in `GamePresence`.

Then, handling the `tab_id` parameter.  If the client provides a `tab_id`, I should use it as the `@connection_id`. If it's not provided, I will generate a unique ID. That way, if a tab was previously using HTTP fallback polling with the same `tab_id`, `GamePresence.register` can seamlessly take over the same connection without accidentally double-counting connections.

What if the game *ends* while a player is connected? My `heartbeat` method needs to handle that. If the game has ended, I should not re-register the player's presence. I just need to transmit the "ended" state. Now, I have to be careful with that `heartbeat` method: I don't want it hammering the SQLite database every few seconds with hundreds of players! The solution?  The `heartbeat` method will ONLY touch `GamePresence` in memory, and zero database queries. On the client side, as soon as it receives the "ended" status, the client will stop its heartbeat timer and unsubscribe.  That's the ticket! That keeps it completely zero-DB on the server.

Next up, the security of `Game.find_signed` and `Player.find_signed`. What if someone tampers with or uses an expired token? It's essential that these functions return `nil` in those cases, so I'll be sure to `reject` the connection.

And, I have to cover the case where the `subscribed` method is called, but the game has already been deleted! In that event, `find_signed` will return `nil`, which means I `reject` it.

Alright, with those details ironed out, I'm ready to create these `app/channels/` files.

cat <<'EOF' > app/channels/moderator_game_channel.rb
class ModeratorGameChannel < ApplicationCable::Channel
  def subscribed
    @game = Game.find_signed(params[:token], purpose: :moderator_channel)
    return reject unless @game

    stream_from Game.moderator_stream_name(@game.id)
    transmit @game.moderator_state
  end

  def resync
    return unless @game

    @game.reload
    transmit @game.moderator_state
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    reject
  end
end
EOF

cat <<'EOF' > app/channels/player_game_channel.rb
class PlayerGameChannel < ApplicationCable::Channel
  def subscribed
    @player = Player.find_signed(params[:token], purpose: :player_channel)
    return reject unless @player

    @game = @player.game
    @connection_id = params[:tab_id].to_s.strip.presence || SecureRandom.uuid
    @tracked = false

    stream_from Game.players_stream_name(@game.id)
    stream_from Game.player_stream_name(@game.id, @player.id)

    unless @game.ended?
      count, changed = GamePresence.register(@game.id, @player.id, @connection_id)
      @tracked = true
      @game.broadcast_presence!(count) if changed
    end

    transmit @game.player_state(@player)
  end

  def unsubscribed
    return unless @tracked && @game && @player && @connection_id

    @tracked = false
    count, changed = GamePresence.unregister(@game.id, @player.id, @connection_id)
    @game.broadcast_presence!(count) if changed
  end

  def heartbeat
    return unless @tracked && @game && @player && @connection_id

    count, changed = GamePresence.heartbeat(@game.id, @player.id, @connection_id)
    @game.broadcast_presence!(count) if changed
  end

  def resync
    return unless @game && @player

    @game.reload
    transmit @game.player_state(@player)
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
    reject
  end
end
EOF

class JoinStatusChannel < ApplicationCable::Channel

    @game = Game.find_by_code(params[:code])
    return reject unless @game

    stream_from Game.join_status_stream_name(@game.id)
    transmit({ type: "state", status: "ended" }) if @game.ended?
  end
end
EOF

cat <<'EOF' > app/controllers/play_controller.rb
class PlayController < ApplicationController
  before_action :disable_caching
  before_action :set_game
  before_action :set_player

  def show
    if @game.ended?
      render :show
    elsif @player
      @player_stream_token = @player.stream_token
      @initial_state = @game.player_state(@player)
      render :show
    else
      @player_form = @game.players.build
      render :show
    end
  end

  def join
    if @game.ended? || @player
      redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other
      return
    end

    @player_form = @game.players.build(name: params.dig(:player, :name).to_s)
    if @player_form.save
      cookies.signed[player_cookie_key(@game)] = {
        value: @player_form.token,
        httponly: true,
        same_site: :lax,
        path: "/",
        expires: 30.days.from_now
      }
      redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other
    else
      render :show, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end
  end

  def answer
    unless @player
      render json: { ok: false, error: "Not joined" }, status: :unauthorized
      return
    end

    result = @game.record_answer!(
      player: @player,
      game_question_id: params[:game_question_id],
      game_option_id: params[:game_option_id]
    )

    if result[:ok]
      render json: result, status: :ok
    else
      render json: result, status: :conflict
    end
  end

  def state
    if @game.ended?
      render json: { type: "state", status: "ended" }
      return
    end

    unless @player
      render json: { type: "unjoined", status: @game.status }, status: :unauthorized
      return
    end

    fallback_client_id = request.headers["X-Quizzy-Fallback-Client"].to_s.strip
    if fallback_client_id.present?
      count, changed = GamePresence.heartbeat(
        @game.id,
        @player.id,
        fallback_client_id,
        ttl: GamePresence::HTTP_FALLBACK_TTL
      )
      @game.broadcast_presence!(count) if changed
    end

    render json: @game.player_state(@player)
  end

  private

  def set_game
    @game = Game.includes(:quiz, game_questions: :game_options).find_by_code(params[:code])
    head :not_found unless @game
  end

  def set_player
    return unless @game

    token = cookies.signed[player_cookie_key(@game)]
    @player = token.present? ? @game.players.find_by(token: token) : nil
  end

  def player_cookie_key(game)
    "quizzy_player_#{game.code}"
  end

  def disable_caching
    response.headers["Cache-Control"] = "no-store"
  end
end
EOF

    assert_not game.finish_question!
    assert_not game.next_question!

    assert_equal "question", game.status
    assert_equal 1, game.current_question_position
    assert_not game.start!

    assert game.finish_question!(expected_position: 1)
    assert_equal "reveal", game.status

    assert_not game.next_question!(expected_position: 2)

    opt1, opt2 = gq1.game_options.to_a

    assert res1[:ok]
    assert_equal 1, game.answers.count
    assert_equal opt1.id, game.answers.first.game_option_id

    # Change pick -> last pick wins, still 1 answer

    assert res2[:ok]
    assert_equal 1, game.answers.count
    assert_equal opt2.id, game.answers.first.game_option_id

    end

require "test_helper"

class GamePresenceTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "tracks distinct players across multiple tabs and isolates games" do
    count, changed = GamePresence.register(10, 100, "tab-1")
    assert_equal 1, count
    assert changed

    # Same player in second tab does not double-count
    count, changed = GamePresence.register(10, 100, "tab-2")
    assert_equal 1, count
    assert_not changed

    assert changed_other
    assert_equal 2, GamePresence.player_count(10)

    # Closing one of Alice's two tabs keeps count at 2
    count, changed = GamePresence.unregister(10, 100, "tab-1")
    assert_equal 2, count
    assert_not changed

    # Closing Alice's second tab drops count to 1

    assert_equal 1, count

end

**System Test Strategy: Capybara and Multi-Browser Chromium**

Okay, all 34 model and integration tests have passed – that's a great start! Now, I need to focus on the comprehensive system tests. The goal is to build out `test/system/live_game_system_test.rb` to rigorously validate *every* real-time interaction across multiple independent browsers. The key here is simulating the interactions WITHOUT page reloads.

But, hold on. Before I dive in, I need to double-check something crucial about the Capybara setup with Cuprite and the `using_session` method. I've configured the `ApplicationSystemTestCase` to set an `Authorization` header for the default session, presumably for the moderator interface.

Aha! Now I see. When I use `Capybara.using_session(:alice) do ... end`, Capybara actually spins up a *completely new* Chromium browser instance! And, importantly, this new instance for `:alice` does **not** inherit the `Authorization` header. That means I can truly simulate independent unauthenticated users with `:alice`, `:bob`, `:charlie`, and `:dave` as if they were entirely separate phones. The default session becomes the authenticated moderator view!

The key is to remember that I need to either call `Capybara.using_session(:alice) { visit "about:blank" }` or let Capybara reset sessions properly to avoid WebSockets lingering from one test to the next, which is a common gotcha!

Alright, with that clarified, I'm ready to write the `test/system/live_game_system_test.rb` file and execute `bin/rails test:system`! Let's get to it.

require "application_system_test_case"

class LiveGameSystemTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  setup do
    @quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Ruby Conf Live")

    @q1 = @quiz.questions.build(body: "Which HTTP status means Too Many Requests?", active: true)
    assert @q1.save_with_options([
      { title: "418", correct: false },
      { title: "429", correct: true },
      { title: "503", correct: false }
    ])

    @q_inactive = @quiz.questions.build(body: "This inactive question must be skipped", active: false)
    assert @q_inactive.save_with_options([
      { title: "Skip A", correct: true },
      { title: "Skip B", correct: false }
    ])

    @q2 = @quiz.questions.build(body: "Which protocols support full-duplex?", active: true)
    assert @q2.save_with_options([
      { title: "WebSocket", correct: true },
      { title: "HTTP/2", correct: true },
      { title: "SMTP", correct: false }
    ])
  end

  test "full live game across moderator and multiple phones without page reloads" do
    # Moderator opens quiz page and starts a game
    visit moderate_quiz_path(@quiz)
    click_button "Start a game"

    assert_match %r{\A/moderate/games/\d+\z}, current_path
    assert_text "Ruby Conf Live"
    assert_text "Players: 0"
    assert_button "Start"

    join_url = find(".lobby__url").text.strip
    assert_match %r{\Ahttp://127\.0\.0\.1:\d+/play/[A-Z0-9]{5}\z}, join_url

    # Verify the join link is plain text (not an <a> tag) and QR SVG exists and matches the join URL
    assert_no_selector ".lobby__url a"
    assert_selector ".qr svg path"
    expected_svg_path = Nokogiri::XML(RQRCode::QRCode.new(join_url).as_svg(
      color: "000000", fill: "ffffff", shape_rendering: "crispEdges",
      module_size: 6, offset: 24, standalone: true, use_path: true, viewbox: true
    )).at_css("path")["d"]
    actual_svg_path = find(".qr svg path", visible: :all)["d"]
    assert_equal expected_svg_path, actual_svg_path

    # Alice joins on her phone (separate unauthenticated browser session)
    Capybara.using_session(:alice) do
      visit join_url
      assert_field "Your name"
      assert_button "Join"
      fill_in "Your name", with: "Alice"
      click_button "Join"
      assert_text "Hi, Alice!"
    end

    # Moderator big screen updates LIVE to Players: 1 (no reload!)
    assert_text "Players: 1"

    # Bob joins on his phone
    Capybara.using_session(:bob) do
      visit join_url
      fill_in "Your name", with: "Bob"
      click_button "Join"
      assert_text "Hi, Bob!"
    end

    # Moderator big screen updates LIVE to Players: 2
    assert_text "Players: 2"

    # Moderator clicks Start -> Question 1 of 2 (inactive question is skipped!)
    click_button "Start"
    assert_text "Question 1 of 2"
    assert_text "Which HTTP status means Too Many Requests?"
    assert_text "418"
    assert_text "429"
    assert_text "503"
    assert_text "Answers: 0 / 2"
    assert_button "Finish"
    assert_no_text "Correct"

    # Alice and Bob see Question 1 LIVE without reload; no correct answer leaked in source!
    Capybara.using_session(:alice) do
      assert_text "Which HTTP status means Too Many Requests?"
      assert_button "418"
      assert_button "429"
      assert_button "503"

      # Security check: page HTML source must not expose correct answer before Finish
      html = page.html
      assert_no_match(/"correct"\s*:\s*true/i, html)
      assert_no_match(/is-correct/i, html)

      # Alice first picks wrong answer 418 -> marked "Your answer"
      click_button "418"
      within("button.play-option", text: "418") do
        assert_text "Your answer"
      end
    end

    # Moderator sees Answers: 1 / 2 LIVE
    assert_text "Answers: 1 / 2"

    # Alice changes her mind to 429 -> last pick counts, still 1 / 2
    Capybara.using_session(:alice) do
      click_button "429"
      within("button.play-option", text: "429") do
        assert_text "Your answer"
      end
      within("button.play-option", text: "418") do
        assert_no_text "Your answer"
      end
    end

    assert_text "Answers: 1 / 2"

    # Charlie joins mid-question! Immediately sees Q1 and can answer!
    Capybara.using_session(:charlie) do
      visit join_url
      fill_in "Your name", with: "Charlie"
      click_button "Join"
      assert_text "Which HTTP status means Too Many Requests?"
      click_button "418"
      within("button.play-option", text: "418") do
        assert_text "Your answer"
      end
    end

    # Moderator sees Answers: 2 / 3 LIVE (Alice + Charlie answered, Bob connected)
    assert_text "Answers: 2 / 3"

    # Moderator clicks Finish -> closes Q1, shows counts & "Correct"
    click_button "Finish"
    within("ol.stage-options li", text: "418") do
      assert_text "1"
      assert_no_text "Correct"
    end
    within("ol.stage-options li", text: "429") do
      assert_text "1"
      assert_text "Correct"
    end
    within("ol.stage-options li", text: "503") do
      assert_text "0"
      assert_no_text "Correct"
    end
    assert_button "Next"
    assert_no_button "End quiz"

    # Phones update LIVE: Alice -> Correct!, Charlie -> Wrong!, Bob -> No answer
    Capybara.using_session(:alice) do
      assert_text "Correct!"
    end
    Capybara.using_session(:charlie) do
      assert_text "Wrong!"
      assert_no_text "Correct!"
    end
    Capybara.using_session(:bob) do
      assert_text "No answer"
      assert_no_text "Correct!"
    end

    # Moderator clicks Next -> skips inactive question -> shows Question 2 of 2
    click_button "Next"
    assert_text "Question 2 of 2"
    assert_text "Which protocols support full-duplex?"
    assert_no_text "This inactive question must be skipped"
    assert_text "Answers: 0 / 3"
    assert_button "Finish"

    # Alice picks WebSocket (correct #1), Bob picks HTTP/2 (correct #2)
    Capybara.using_session(:alice) do
      assert_text "Which protocols support full-duplex?"
      click_button "WebSocket"
      within("button.play-option", text: "WebSocket") { assert_text "Your answer" }
    end
    Capybara.using_session(:bob) do
      assert_text "Which protocols support full-duplex?"
      click_button "HTTP/2"
      within("button.play-option", text: "HTTP/2") { assert_text "Your answer" }
    end

    assert_text "Answers: 2 / 3"

    # Moderator clicks Finish on last question -> both correct options marked "Correct", button is "End quiz"
    click_button "Finish"
    within("ol.stage-options li", text: "WebSocket") do
      assert_text "1"
      assert_text "Correct"
    end
    within("ol.stage-options li", text: "HTTP/2") do
      assert_text "1"
      assert_text "Correct"
    end
    within("ol.stage-options li", text: "SMTP") do
      assert_text "0"
      assert_no_text "Correct"
    end
    assert_button "End quiz"
    assert_no_button "Next"

    Capybara.using_session(:alice) { assert_text "Correct!" }
    Capybara.using_session(:bob) { assert_text "Correct!" }
    Capybara.using_session(:charlie) { assert_text "No answer" }

    # Moderator clicks End quiz -> big screen and all phones show "The quiz is over" LIVE
    click_button "End quiz"
    assert_text "The quiz is over"

    Capybara.using_session(:alice) { assert_text "The quiz is over" }
    Capybara.using_session(:bob) { assert_text "The quiz is over" }
    Capybara.using_session(:charlie) { assert_text "The quiz is over" }

    # New visitor cannot join after end
    Capybara.using_session(:dave) do
      visit join_url
      assert_text "The quiz is over"
      assert_no_field "Your name"
      assert_no_button "Join"
    end
  end

  test "live presence updates when players leave or open multiple tabs and browser remembers player" do
    visit moderate_quiz_path(@quiz)
    click_button "Start a game"
    join_url = find(".lobby__url").text.strip
    assert_text "Players: 0"

    # Alice joins
    Capybara.using_session(:alice_presence) do
      visit join_url
      fill_in "Your name", with: "Alice"
      click_button "Join"
      assert_text "Hi, Alice!"
    end
    assert_text "Players: 1"

    # Bob joins
    Capybara.using_session(:bob_presence) do
      visit join_url
      fill_in "Your name", with: "Bob"
      click_button "Join"
      assert_text "Hi, Bob!"
    end
    assert_text "Players: 2"

    # Alice opens the join link in a SECOND tab in the same browser -> remembered, NOT double-counted!
    second_tab = nil
    Capybara.using_session(:alice_presence) do
      second_tab = open_new_window
      within_window(second_tab) do
        visit join_url
        assert_text "Hi, Alice!"
        assert_no_field "Your name"
      end
    end
    # Wait briefly and verify count stays 2
    assert_text "Players: 2"

    # Alice closes her second tab -> still connected on first tab -> stays 2
    Capybara.using_session(:alice_presence) do
      second_tab.close
    end
    assert_text "Players: 2"

    # Bob leaves the page -> count drops LIVE to 1!
    Capybara.using_session(:bob_presence) do
      visit "/"
    end
    assert_text "Players: 1"

    # Moderator starts question -> Answers: 0 / 1
    click_button "Start"
    assert_text "Answers: 0 / 1"

    # Alice answers -> Answers: 1 / 1
    Capybara.using_session(:alice_presence) do
      assert_text "Which HTTP status means Too Many Requests?"
      click_button "429"
      within("button.play-option", text: "429") { assert_text "Your answer" }
    end
    assert_text "Answers: 1 / 1"

    # Bob returns to join link in same browser -> remembered as Bob, sees open question, count becomes 1 / 2!
    Capybara.using_session(:bob_presence) do
      visit join_url
      assert_no_field "Your name"
      assert_text "Hi, Bob!"
      assert_text "Which HTTP status means Too Many Requests?"
    end
    assert_text "Answers: 1 / 2"

    # Both players leave -> second counter drops to 0 ("are there any active players in the game")
    Capybara.using_session(:bob_presence) { visit "/" }
    assert_text "Answers: 1 / 1"
    Capybara.using_session(:alice_presence) { visit "/" }
    assert_text "Answers: 1 / 0"

    # Alice opens join link again -> remembered with her earlier answer STILL marked "Your answer"!
    Capybara.using_session(:alice_presence) do
      visit join_url
      assert_no_field "Your name"
      assert_text "Hi, Alice!"
      within("button.play-option", text: "429") { assert_text "Your answer" }
    end
    assert_text "Answers: 1 / 1"
  end

  test "multiple games of same quiz are isolated and reconnecting player syncs missed transitions" do
    # Game 1: single active question (deactivate q2 temporarily)
    @q2.update!(active: false)

    visit moderate_quiz_path(@quiz)
    click_button "Start a game"
    game1_url = find(".lobby__url").text.strip

    Capybara.using_session(:reconnect_player) do
      visit game1_url
      fill_in "Your name", with: "Alice"
      click_button "Join"
      assert_text "Hi, Alice!"
    end
    assert_text "Players: 1"

    # Single active question -> Question 1 of 1 -> Finish -> End quiz directly
    click_button "Start"
    assert_text "Question 1 of 1"
    click_button "Finish"
    assert_button "End quiz"
    assert_no_button "Next"
    click_button "End quiz"
    assert_text "The quiz is over"

    Capybara.using_session(:reconnect_player) do
      assert_text "The quiz is over"
    end

    # Re-activate q2 and start Game 2 of the same quiz
    @q2.update!(active: true)
    click_link "← Back to quiz"
    click_button "Start a game"
    game2_url = find(".lobby__url").text.strip
    assert_not_equal game1_url, game2_url
    assert_text "Players: 0"

    # Same browser visits Game 2 -> asked for name fresh (new game = new players!)
    Capybara.using_session(:reconnect_player) do
      visit game2_url
      assert_field "Your name"
      fill_in "Your name", with: "Alice Rehearsal 2"
      click_button "Join"
      assert_text "Hi, Alice Rehearsal 2!"

      # Simulate flaky conference Wi-Fi drop by closing ActionCable connection while moderator advances!
      page.execute_script(<<~JS)
        const el = document.querySelector("[data-controller='player-game']")
        const ctrl = window.Stimulus.getControllerForElementAndIdentifier(el, "player-game")
        ctrl.consumer.connection.close({ allowReconnect: true })
      JS
    end

    # Moderator starts Q1, finishes Q1, and moves to Q2 while phone recovers!
    click_button "Start"
    click_button "Finish"
    click_button "Next"
    assert_text "Question 2 of 2"

    # Phone automatically reconnects (without page reload!) and syncs to Question 2 of 2!
    Capybara.using_session(:reconnect_player) do
      assert_text "Which protocols support full-duplex?", wait: 10
      click_button "WebSocket"
      within("button.play-option", text: "WebSocket") { assert_text "Your answer" }
    end

    assert_text "Answers: 1 / 1", wait: 10
  end
end
EOF

steps.message: Aha! Found the root cause right away in `log/test.log`: `Importmap skipped missing path: controllers/..._controller.js` because stale precompiled assets exist in `public/assets/`. Let me check `public/assets` and clobber them!
steps.reasoning_content:
**Eureka! Manifest Malfunction!**

Whoa, hold everything! I need to zoom in on lines 14337-14339 in that log file *immediately*! It's screaming at me! "Importmap skipped missing path:..." Three times, the same pattern: controller files are being skipped!

BINGO! I think I see the problem! *Hahahaha*! It's so clear now. It looks like `public/assets/.manifest.json` was already hanging around from a *previous* precompile, the one before we added the new JavaScript files. So, the `Propshaft` gem, operating in its `test` mode, was reading this *stale* precompiled manifest in `public/assets/` rather than compiling *our* new JavaScript files. This explains why Importmap was not working as expected! Time to confirm that suspicion by listing the contents of `public/assets`!

arguments.command: ls -la public/assets && bin/rails assets:clobber && bin/rails test:system test/system/live_game_system_test.rb

Wow, that was a spectacular start! All eleven system tests, including every single live multi-browser test, passed on the very first run with zero failures and zero errors! That's `11 runs, 317 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skips`! And, just to be sure, `bin/serve` runs `bin/rails assets:clobber assets:precompile`! So, the production environment will have fresh assets. But, as we both know, a successful initial run is only the beginning. This is where the *real* work starts. Now, let's dive deep into those critical edge cases.

First, I need to focus on some truly devilish scenarios. We'll inspect the real, rendered app and test `bin/serve` in `RAILS_ENV=production`. Let's create some hostile/flaky Wi-Fi scenarios to test, and don't forget the QR code rasterization/decoding. Security is paramount, and so we will check RuboCop & Brakeman. We'll scrutinize every single line to ensure nothing escapes our notice!

Here are some edge cases I'm going to add to the system tests right now:

1.  **Duplicate Tab Interaction:** I want to verify that when a player has two tabs open with the same player, answering in Tab 1 updates Tab 2 live. I need to make sure that when a moderator clicks "Finish", BOTH tabs show "Correct!"
2.  **Pre-Join Scenarios:** We need to test the scenario where a player sits on the join page *before* joining. If the moderator clicks "End quiz", does the open join page switch live to "The quiz is over" and hide the join form? I'll need to really test the functionality of our `JoinStatusChannel` + `join_status_controller.js`.
3.  **Offline Answer Handling:** I need to simulate a Wi-Fi drop (via fetch failure or CDP offline). When a player taps an option while offline, does the answer automatically retry and succeed when the network recovers, updating the moderator's "Answers: 1 / 1"? What if the moderator clicks "Finish" while the player is still offline? Does the player sync to "No answer" and *not* falsely claim "Correct!"?
4.  **Zero-Question Game Start:** What happens when the moderator attempts to start a game on a quiz with no active questions? Does it redirect back cleanly with an alert, and does toggling a question "Active" then allow the game to start correctly?
5.  **Reloading State Preservation:** Does reloading the big-screen page in the middle of an open question, during reveal, and after the end, preserve the exact state, counts, progress, options, "Correct" badges, and continue receiving live updates afterward?
6.  **Mid-Game Join During Reveal:** Does the player opening `/play/:code` during a reveal mid-game see "No answer" immediately? And when the moderator clicks "Next", does it smoothly transition live?
7.  **Channel Security:** Isolate action cable channels and write unit tests to verify: Can someone subscribe to `ModeratorGameChannel` with a player's token or a forged/blank token? MUST be rejected! And what about `PlayerGameChannel`?
8.  **Production Serve Verification:** Let's run a full-blown production test! Start `bin/serve` in `RAILS_ENV=production` on a separate port with the necessary environment variables! We'll verify the `/up` endpoint returns `200`! Does plain HTTP work? Does ActionCable WebSockets work in *production* mode? And we'll verify there are zero JS console errors and network failures.

require "test_helper"

class GameChannelsTest < ActionCable::Channel::TestCase
  setup do
    @quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Channel Security Quiz")
    q = @quiz.questions.build(body: "Is Ruby fun?", active: true)
    assert q.save_with_options([
      { title: "Yes", correct: true },
      { title: "No", correct: false }
    ])
    @game = Game.create_for_quiz!(@quiz)
    @player = @game.players.create!(name: "Alice")
  end

  test "ModeratorGameChannel rejects missing, forged, or player tokens and accepts valid moderator token" do
    self.class.tests ModeratorGameChannel

    subscribe
    assert subscription.rejected?

    subscribe(token: "forged-token")
    assert subscription.rejected?

    # Player's signed token must NOT grant access to ModeratorGameChannel
    subscribe(token: @player.stream_token)
    assert subscription.rejected?

    subscribe(token: @game.moderator_stream_token)
    assert subscription.confirmed?
    assert_has_stream Game.moderator_stream_name(@game.id)
    assert_equal "lobby", transmissions.last["status"]
  end

  test "PlayerGameChannel rejects invalid or moderator tokens, tracks presence, and never leaks correct before reveal" do
    self.class.tests PlayerGameChannel

    subscribe
    assert subscription.rejected?

    subscribe(token: @game.moderator_stream_token)
    assert subscription.rejected?

    @game.start!
    subscribe(token: @player.stream_token, tab_id: "tab-a")
    assert subscription.confirmed?
    assert_has_stream Game.players_stream_name(@game.id)
    assert_has_stream Game.player_stream_name(@game.id, @player.id)
    assert_equal 1, GamePresence.player_count(@game.id)

    payload = transmissions.last
    assert_equal "question", payload["status"]
    payload["question"]["options"].each do |opt|
      assert_not opt.key?("correct")
    end

    unsubscribe
    assert_equal 0, GamePresence.player_count(@game.id)
  end

  test "JoinStatusChannel streams join status without registering presence" do
    self.class.tests JoinStatusChannel

    subscribe(code: "NOPE1")
    assert subscription.rejected?

    subscribe(code: @game.code)
    assert subscription.confirmed?
    assert_has_stream Game.join_status_stream_name(@game.id)
    assert_equal 0, GamePresence.player_count(@game.id)
  end
end
EOF

class LiveGameEdgeCasesSystemTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  setup do
    @quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Edge Case Conf")
    @q1 = @quiz.questions.build(body: "First question?", active: true)
    assert @q1.save_with_options([
      { title: "Yes", correct: true },
      { title: "No", correct: false }
    ])
    @q2 = @quiz.questions.build(body: "Second question?", active: true)
    assert @q2.save_with_options([
      { title: "Alpha", correct: false },
      { title: "Beta", correct: true }
    ])
  end

  test "zero active questions alerts cleanly, toggling active allows starting, reload preserves state, join during reveal and live end on join form" do
    @quiz.questions.update_all(active: false)

    visit moderate_quiz_path(@quiz)
    click_button "Start a game"
    assert_text "Activate at least one question before starting a game."
    assert_current_path moderate_quiz_path(@quiz)

    # Toggle both questions active via AJAX checkboxes without reloading
    within("ol.question-list > li", text: "First question?") { check "Active" }
    within("ol.question-list > li", text: "Second question?") { check "Active" }
    assert_text "2 of 2 questions active"

    click_button "Start a game"
    join_url = find(".lobby__url").text.strip

    # Visitor Eve sits on the join form WITHOUT joining yet
    Capybara.using_session(:eve_unjoined) do
      visit join_url
      assert_field "Your name"
      assert_button "Join"
    end

    # Presence must STILL be 0 because Eve has NOT joined!
    assert_text "Players: 0"

    # Alice joins and opens a second tab to verify cross-tab answer sync
    alice_tab2 = nil
    Capybara.using_session(:alice_sync) do
      visit join_url
      fill_in "Your name", with: "Alice"
      click_button "Join"
      assert_text "Hi, Alice!"
      alice_tab2 = open_new_window
      within_window(alice_tab2) do
        visit join_url
        assert_text "Hi, Alice!"
      end
    end
    assert_text "Players: 1"

    # Start Q1 -> Alice answers in Tab 1 -> Tab 2 updates live!
    click_button "Start"
    assert_text "Answers: 0 / 1"

    Capybara.using_session(:alice_sync) do
      assert_text "First question?"
      click_button "Yes"
      within("button.play-option", text: "Yes") { assert_text "Your answer" }

      within_window(alice_tab2) do
        assert_text "First question?"
        within("button.play-option", text: "Yes") { assert_text "Your answer" }
      end
    end
    assert_text "Answers: 1 / 1"

    # Moderator reloads the big screen mid-question -> state & counter preserved and live updates continue!
    visit current_path
    assert_text "Question 1 of 2"
    assert_text "First question?"
    assert_text "Answers: 1 / 1"
    assert_button "Finish"

    # Moderator clicks Finish -> both of Alice's tabs show Correct!
    click_button "Finish"
    within("ol.stage-options li", text: "Yes") do
      assert_text "1"
      assert_text "Correct"
    end

    Capybara.using_session(:alice_sync) do
      assert_text "Correct!"
      within_window(alice_tab2) { assert_text "Correct!" }
      alice_tab2.close
    end

    # Frank joins DURING reveal -> immediately sees "No answer", then advances to Q2 live!
    Capybara.using_session(:frank_reveal) do
      visit join_url
      fill_in "Your name", with: "Frank"
      click_button "Join"
      assert_text "No answer"
    end

    # Moderator reloads during reveal -> still reveal with Next button
    visit current_path
    assert_text "Question 1 of 2"
    assert_button "Next"

    # Advance to Q2 -> Frank and Alice update live
    click_button "Next"
    assert_text "Question 2 of 2"
    assert_text "Answers: 0 / 2"

    # Simulate brief network error on Frank's answer tap (fails once, then succeeds on retry!)
    Capybara.using_session(:frank_reveal) do
      assert_text "Second question?"
      page.execute_script(<<~JS)
        const origFetch = window.fetch
        let failedOnce = false
        window.fetch = function(...args) {
          if (!failedOnce && String(args[0]).includes("/answer")) {
            failedOnce = true
            return Promise.reject(new TypeError("Simulated Wi-Fi hiccup"))
          }
          return origFetch.apply(this, args)
        }
      JS
      click_button "Beta"
      within("button.play-option", text: "Beta") { assert_text "Your answer" }
    end

    # Retry succeeds within ~1s and moderator sees Answers: 1 / 2!
    assert_text "Answers: 1 / 2", wait: 10

    click_button "Finish"
    Capybara.using_session(:frank_reveal) { assert_text "Correct!" }

    click_button "End quiz"
    assert_text "The quiz is over"

    # Even Eve's unjoined join-form page switches live to "The quiz is over"!
    Capybara.using_session(:eve_unjoined) do
      assert_text "The quiz is over"
      assert_no_button "Join"
    end
  end
end

Okay, here's the plan. That's fantastic news – every single one of those tests passed! That's a good foundation, but now we need to put it to the real test. We're going to fire up the production environment using `bin/serve` in `RAILS_ENV=production`. We'll set it to run on port 3099, and simulate a real-world scenario with Chromium controlling both a moderator and a player. We're going to hit `http://localhost:3099` hard and verify EVERYTHING.

First, let's confirm `bin/serve` spins up cleanly in production, using SQLite in `storage/production.sqlite3`, and that asset precompilation works as expected. Then, we need a 200 response on `/up`. Plain HTTP should work with custom Host headers without any redirects – that's crucial. Next, we'll have the moderator create and start a game, and then launch the big screen on `http://localhost:3099`.

We’re keeping an eagle eye on browser JS consoles for errors and on network responses for any 404s or 500s. We need the "Players: 1" and "Answers: 1 / 1" texts to be clean, single-line text elements. Now, the real test: WebSocket `/cable` upgrades must work flawlessly in production over plain HTTP, `ws://localhost:3099/cable`. Live updates need to flow end-to-end without any page reloads.

Finally, we'll clean up the temporary production SQLite DB afterwards. I'm trying to decide how we should handle the public/assets directory, whether to leave it clobbered or precompiled. Since `bin/serve` runs `bin/rails assets:clobber assets:precompile` at startup, and `bin/rails test:system` fails if stale `public/assets` exists, I'm leaning toward precompiling AFTER all edits. That way, `public/assets` has our latest assets. Or, maybe clobbering is even better? Let's check `.gitignore` and how the repo was when we started all this, just to be certain.

cat <<'EOF' > docs/architecture.md
# Quizzy Architecture & Design Notes

## Runtime & Deployment

- **Entrypoint**: `bin/serve` prepares SQLite (`bin/rails db:prepare`), compiles Propshaft assets (`bin/rails assets:clobber assets:precompile`), and runs Puma in the foreground listening on `0.0.0.0:${PORT}`.
- **Plain HTTP & Host Independence**: `config.assume_ssl = false`, `config.force_ssl = false`, `config.hosts.clear`, `config.public_file_server.enabled = true`, and ActionCable's `allow_same_origin_as_host = true` ensure the app works over plain HTTP on any conference network hostname without external dependencies.
- **Storage & Concurrency**: All persistent state lives under `storage/` (`storage/production.sqlite3`, WAL mode with `foreign_keys = ON`). `config/database.yml` sizes `max_connections` to `RAILS_MAX_THREADS + 10` so Puma threads (`5`) and ActionCable worker pool threads never starve under conference load.
- **Health Check**: `GET /up` returns `200` without authentication.

## Authentication & Authorization

- All moderator routes live under `/moderate` and inherit from `Moderate::BaseController`.
- `Moderate::BaseController` enforces HTTP Basic Authentication comparing against `ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME"]` and `ENV["QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD"]` using SHA-256 digests with `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`. Empty credentials are always rejected (`401`).
- Public player routes (`/play/:code`, `/play/:code/join`, `/play/:code/answer`, `/play/:code/state`) inherit directly from `ApplicationController` and require no account or moderator credentials.
- ActionCable channels authorize per-channel via Rails `ActiveRecord::SignedId` tokens with distinct purposes (`:moderator_channel` on `Game`, `:player_channel` on `Player`) so players cannot subscribe to moderator streams or other players' streams.

## Data Model

### Quiz Authoring
- `Quiz` (`quizzes`): `title` (required, whitespace-normalized). `has_many :games, dependent: :destroy`, `has_many :questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy`.
- `Question` (`questions`): `quiz_id`, `body`, `position`, `active` (default `true`). `has_many :options, dependent: :destroy`, `has_many :game_questions, dependent: :nullify`.
- `Option` (`options`): `question_id`, `title`, `correct` (default `false`), `position`.
- `Question#save_with_options` validates `body` and non-empty option rows (>= 2 options, >= 1 correct) before touching the DB.
- `Question#move!(direction)` atomically swaps adjacent positions and normalizes `1..N`.

### Live Games (Snapshotted per Run)
- `Game` (`games`): `quiz_id`, `code` (unique 5-char uppercase unambiguous code, e.g. `K7RZX`), `status` (`lobby` -> `question` -> `reveal` -> `ended`), `current_question_position`, `started_at`, `ended_at`.
  - `Game.create_for_quiz!(quiz)` snapshots only active questions (in position order) into `GameQuestion` and their options into `GameOption`. Inactive questions are skipped, and later edits/deletes on `Question`/`Option` never break or corrupt past/running games.
  - State transitions (`start!`, `finish_question!`, `next_question!`, `end_game!`) use atomic conditional `update_all` guards (with optional `expected_position`) inside transactions so accidental double-clicks cannot skip questions.
- `GameQuestion` (`game_questions`): `game_id`, `question_id` (nullable, `on_delete: :nullify`), `body`, `position`.
- `GameOption` (`game_options`): `game_question_id`, `title`, `correct`, `position`.
- `Player` (`players`): `game_id`, `name` (whitespace-normalized, duplicate names allowed), `token` (unique random token persisted in a per-game signed HttpOnly cookie `quizzy_player_#{code}` so reopening the join link in the same browser continues as the same player).
- `Answer` (`answers`): `game_id`, `player_id`, `game_question_id`, `game_option_id`, unique index on `[player_id, game_question_id]`. `Game#record_answer!` uses `Answer.upsert` so players can change their pick while a question is open and the last pick counts; submissions after `"Finish"` are rejected with `409` and return the authoritative server state.

### Security Invariant (Answer Confidentiality)
- `Game#player_broadcast_state` and `Game#player_state` strictly omit `correct` flags while `status` is `"lobby"` or `"question"`, and only expose the current question's options (never upcoming questions). Neither the initial HTML source, JSON state endpoint, nor WebSocket frames reveal correct answers before `"Finish"`.

## Real-Time Updates, Presence & Conference Wi-Fi Resilience

- **Transport**: ActionCable (`adapter: async` in single-process Puma, `actioncable.esm.js` vendored offline via Importmap) with three channels:
  - `ModeratorGameChannel`: streams `game:#{id}:moderator` (`state`, `presence`, `counts`) and immediately transmits full `moderator_state` on subscribe/reconnect.
  - `PlayerGameChannel`: streams `game:#{id}:players` (shared phase transitions without thundering-herd HTTP refetches on reveal) and `game:#{id}:player:#{player.id}` (cross-tab answer sync), and transmits personalized `player_state` on subscribe/reconnect.
  - `JoinStatusChannel`: lightweight stream on unjoined join pages so they live-switch to `"The quiz is over"` if the game ends before the visitor submits, without counting them as players.
- **Live Presence (`GamePresence`)**:
  - Thread-safe in-memory registry tracking `{ game_id => { player_id => { tab_id => expires_at } } }`.
  - Deduplicates multiple tabs in the same browser under one `player_id`.
  - Decrements immediately on tab close / navigation (`unsubscribed` + `pagehide` disconnect), and evicts silently dropped Wi-Fi connections via client heartbeats (`4s`) and a background reaper (`15s` staleness timeout) with zero DB writes.
- **Flaky Wi-Fi Recovery**:
  - Both `moderator_game_controller.js` and `player_game_controller.js` reconnect aggressively on `disconnected`, `online`, and `visibilitychange`, and automatically fall back to HTTP JSON polling (`GET .../state`) only while WebSocket is disconnected (stopping as soon as WS recovers).
  - `player_game_controller.js` uses single-flight latest-wins answer submission with automatic retry on transient network failures so rapid taps never race out of order and Wi-Fi blips recover cleanly.
  - All live endpoints set `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- **QR Code**: Generated purely server-side as inline SVG via `rqrcode` (`ApplicationHelper#qr_code_svg`) with `#000000` modules, `#ffffff` background `<rect>`, 4-module quiet zone, and `xmlns` — zero external services.

## Quiz Export & Import

- **Export**: `GET /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/export` renders `Quiz#to_export_json` inside `<pre class="code-block">`. Strictly scoped to `title`, `questions`, and `options` — live games/players/answers are never exported.
- **Import**: `GET/POST /moderate/import` uses `QuizImport` to validate the full JSON payload before creating a new `Quiz` atomically.

## Notes for Future Releases (Scores, Leaderboards, Past Games / Responses)

- `games`, `game_questions`, `game_options`, `players`, and `answers` already persist full per-game history (with `started_at`, `ended_at`, per-player answers, and `game_options.correct`) needed for live scoring, leaderboards, winner highlights, and post-game moderator response views.
- `quizzy.css` already includes `.runs-table`, `.badge`, `.leaderboard`, `.leader`, `.result-card`, `.winner-banner`, and `.response-*` styles ready for future features.
EOF
